proof_summary: Direct finite checks show that 43 has the required property and that every integer from 44 through 288 fails it. For \(k\ge289\), write \(k=m^2+s\) with \(m=\lfloor\sqrt{k}\rfloor\) and \(0\le s\le2m\); a case split on \(s\) selects one of the nearby bases \(m,m-1,m-2,m-3\) in which the three-digit expansion of \(k\) has three pairwise distinct digits.
